key_insight: In compressible turbulent advection, Allee-effect population growth can fail when flow-induced sinks concentrate organisms below a critical density, causing extinction above a flow-dependent threshold.
engineering_relevance: This matters for predicting and managing microbial survival, bioreactor performance, and transport-driven population persistence in environments where effective compressibility alters local density.
method: Derive analytical carrying-capacity expressions versus Allee strength in the small- and large-Damköhler-number limits.
Use numerical simulations to connect the asymptotic regimes across intermediate Damköhler numbers.
Relate extinction thresholds to statistics of sinks and sources in fully developed turbulence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical theory plus numerical simulations showing how carrying capacity and a critical Allee-strength threshold depend on Damköhler number and compressible-flow statistics.
watch_item: The extinction threshold is stated for the small-Damköhler, fully developed turbulence limit, so extrapolation to other flow regimes or organism dynamics should be done cautiously.
paper_title: The Allee Effect in Compressible Flows
